[WP] You have been studying the tactics of history's greatest generals in order to free the remaining colonies from the alien oppression.

Notes based on the recently discovered text of the great alien war hero The Duke of Nukem from his Strategy Guide. This tome shows to have been written in AD 2011, nearly six hundred years ago. As far as records show, this was the last known alien incursion.

  1. The aliens have several weak points that we have so far been unaware of. The buttocks of these creatures is apparently made of some sort of cellulose fiber. The Duke often referred to their ass as being made of grass in the literature. In battle, hebrought an old world tool called a weed-eater. We are currently combing records for information on how to create this great weapon. This could lead to discovering more effective methods for dispatching our enemy.
  2. A substance called “Bubble Gum” was used by warriors prior to entering combat. Whether this allowed some sort of immunity to their nerve disrupting saliva or not is yet to be seen. It is noted that as The Duke charged into battle he would let them know that he both came to “kick ass (a reference to the previous cellulose structure discovery) and chew bubble gum . . . and he was all out of bubble gum.” Something about this substance is absolutely necessary before we engage the enemy. We are also searching the archives for any mention of this “Bubble Gum” so we can effectively recreate it.
  3. The Duke of Nukem quite often referred to his “balls of steel.” Could the aliens have some sort of allergic reaction to steel that we are unaware of? We are currently developing prototypes based on old world musket balls to attack the alien insurgency with. If we are lucky, we may have found something new and ground breaking.
  4. We may have found a breakthrough in combating the alien regeneration issue. As many of you know, many of the aliens manage to continue fighting, sometimes growing entire limbs back, after a normal man would be considered dead. The Duke refers to a tactic of “ripping off their head and shitting down their necks” in combat. Granted, we may not have time to stop at each corpse but we plan to issue spray packs to several personnel in each unit that will contain a human feces mixture. We plan to sever the heads of all aliens that we make contact with and liberally apply this mixture to the wound. With all luck this will stop the cellular regeneration. Armed with this knowledge, the alien scum may truly, in the words of The Duke, “eat shit and die” finally.

We will work to rapidly develop these strategies to full battlefield readiness for the next attempt at liberation. Please assign personnel to working on these tasks ASAP as this may be the turning point in the Great War.

You come home from work/school and are exhausted - yet don't feel like ordering in. What are your go-to recipes that are simple? Simple could mean either quick to make, or only few ingredients are needed.

Personally I'm a fan of the classic stir fry. Fry vegetables, add rice. What's easier than that?

OR if I want to feed myself for the next few days, it's homemade soup. Roughly cut veg, add stock, bring to a boil and then simmer for 90 minutes. Salt to taste. I cheat and use pre-made stock though.

How about you guys? What's something you can make with little effort?
What are your favourite simple recipes?

I don't cook anything if it takes more than ten minutes, so I've amassed a few super easy recipes over time. As an added benefit, I feel really sick if my blood sugar is high or low, so these recipes are good for keeping it stable and tend to have a lot of vegetables / be low-calorie per serving.

  1. I invented this recipe, and I call it "Spinach, Chicken and Cheese Mush". Take some frozen spinach, microwave it for 5 minutes to defrost it. Toss on a slice of cheese. Toss in a can of canned chicken (you can't even tell it's canned if you drain it well). Microwave 30 seconds. Mix. Bam, tons of vegetables, high protein, high fat low carb meal, which is good for keeping your blood sugar from spiking then crashing.

  2. Baked potatoes. Wash two potatoes. Poke a bunch of holes in them. Microwave 5 minutes per potato. Cut potatoes open. Insert cheese, tuna fish, whatever you want. Maybe microwave some vegetables too. Bam, done. Not too horrible for you, especially if you freeze a couple of potatoes and reheat them as needed- cooling and reheating potatoes reduces the amount of starch in them, which means more stable blood sugar for you!

  3. Rice and seaweed (if you have a rice cooker). This is NOT really that healthy, but it is quick and tasty. Go to the Asian supermarket and pick up some flavor of snack nori, whatever you like. I have sweet and spicy squid flavored nori right now. Put some sticky rice (or not sticky rice, but I like sticky rice) in the rice cooker. Put in twice that amount of water, or 2.5 times if it's brown rice. Turn on rice cooker. Mix rice with seaweed, or else wrap rice in seaweed. Eat rice with seaweed, and maybe tuna.

  4. Hobo Curry. This is only easy if you have a slapchop type vegetable chopper, but I highly recommend them because they make a one hour job into a one minute job. Chop up a shit ton of vegetables, whatever kind you have. Put them in a pan with oil or butter. Cook them. Then dump in some chicken if you want, again, if it's from a can, it's super easy. Half a cup to a cup of milk depending on the amount of vegetables you added, about two tablespoons of curry powder, maybe some sriracha sauce. Bam, curry. Put it over rice, or else microwave frozen cauliflower and chop it up really small in your vegetable chopper and put it over that. It tastes about the same.

  5. Hobo tzatziki sauce and chicken. One cup of nonfat plain yogurt, 3/4 tablespoon of dill, 2/3 tablespoon garlic powder, about half a cucumber, one tablespoon lemon juice, salt and pepper, some canned chicken (like two cansish). Mix sauce. Put sauce on chicken. Eat.

Can somebody explain this to me please, why is the Chinese sock market tanking? Is it just a correction?
A large correction. Almost double the value in 1 year was never going to be sustainable. It will flow to other markets in massive ways to come.

It's a bubble popping. The most similar event in recent times would be the dot com bubble.

The Chinese government wants to transition from an export economy to a consumer economy. In order to do this, they encouraged people to invest in the stock market. The influx of money caused prices to rise. People saw the rising prices and decided to get in on the action. This pushed prices higher. In the last year, the stock market went from 2000 to 5000. In that same time period, Chinese companies didn't suddenly become 2.5x as profitable. Once new money stopped entering the stock market, prices stopped rising. People sold their stocks and prices started to fall. Then more people sold and price fell further prompting even more people to sell, which caused prices to drop further and more people to sell...
